descriptor.scene: THE BELL. DAVID KOBROSKY stands at the end-of-treatment bell mounted on the clinic wall, one hand on the pull cord mid-RING, his other fist raised, face thrown back in a huge open laugh. His hair is back as a SHORT dark regrowth of curls under no hat. Around him, THREE nurses in scrubs and TWO friends applaud and cheer, all eyes on HIM, one friend holding up a phone to film, another holding a small handmade sign that reads exactly CANCER FREE in marker capitals. Streamers, a balloon, afternoon light. Pure triumph, zero solemnity. Lower-right: clinic floor with a fallen streamer, calm.
descriptor._caption: And here is the most David thing that has ever happened. Mid-chemo, he rallied hundreds of friends to help cover someone else's cancer treatment, and let the internet vote on his hairstyle before the razor took it. By November the scans came back clean. Cancer, meet David. Let me introduce you.
descriptor.anonymous: Three nurses in scrubs and two friends, visibly distinct from David and each other: mixed ages, builds and skin tones; nobody wears sky-blue; nobody resembles David.
negatives: any legible text besides the exact sign CANCER FREE
solemn or tearful tone: this is a victory
